SOURCE: "Harnessing Agentic Evolution" (AEvo). First author Jiayi Zhang (HKUST-Guangzhou, DeepWisdom). Co-authors include Yongfeng Gu, Jianhao Ruan, Bang Liu, Chenglin Wu and Yuyu Luo. Preprint, arXiv:2605.13821v1 [cs.AI], 13 May 2026. No venue.

COVERAGE: All 24 pages and 75,813 chars were read. Skimmed: the reference list (pp. 10-12) and the long code listings in Appendix C (pp. 14-24). The extraction is clean prose, but table columns run together (see PROBLEMS).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: Treat the evolve loop as an interactive environment. The state is the accumulated evolution context. A meta-agent acts by editing the mechanism Π that produces candidates, not by proposing the next candidate. This is the "update the update method" move, made explicit.
  number: none
  setup: Formal definition in Section 3. Applies to procedure-based and agent-based evolution.
  quote: "A meta-agent acts on this environment not by generating the next candidate, but by editing the mechanism that controls how future evolution proceeds."
  where: p.2. Formalism p.4: "Πr+1 = Edit(Πr, ar)".
- Claim: AEvo Procedure beats five procedure-based baselines on Terminal-Bench and ARC-AGI-2, about 26% relative on average over the strongest baseline.
  number: 26%. Terminal-Bench 53.8 against 44.3 for DGM and AFlow. ARC-AGI-2 47.0 against 36.0 for ADAS. One-shot ReAct scores 28.6 and 21.8.
  setup: Gemini-3-Flash executes candidates. Avg@3 over 3 runs. 20 optimization rounds. Meta-agent is Claude Code or Codex on Opus-4.7 or GPT-5.4.
  quote: "yielding a 26% relative improvement over the strongest baseline on average."
  where: p.6, Table 2 on p.7. The 53.8/47.0 split is read from the merged row "AEVO Procedure Gemini-3-Flash53.8747.012".
- Claim: Kernel optimization reached 1138 cycles in 100 iterations, which the authors call the best reported under the same budget. Extending to 200 iterations gave 1121.
  number: 1138 cycles (100 iterations), 1121 (200 iterations). Baselines: Claude Code 1615, Codex 1667, OpenEvolve 2411, HyperAgents 7086 (all Opus-4.7).
  setup: Anthropic performance take-home on a VLIW SIMD simulator. Codex/GPT-5.4 AEvo Agent. Best@3. Lower is better.
  quote: "AEVOachieves 1138 cycles within 100 iterations, which is, to our knowledge, the best reported result under the same iteration budget."
  where: p.6. 200-iteration extension on p.8: "The best result improves from 1138 to 1121 cycles".
- Claim: AEvo costs about 3x the per-round cost of procedure baselines on the standard benchmarks. The authors present this as paying for optimization-time reasoning.
  number: about 3x
  setup: Terminal-Bench and ARC-AGI-2.
  quote: "AEVOcosts about three times as much as procedure-based baselines on these benchmarks."
  where: p.7
- Claim: On open-ended tasks AEvo Agent is cost-competitive, at about $0.32-0.34 per round on circle packing, $1.31-1.40 on autocorrelation and $1.23-1.27 on kernel. Cost is not set by agent versus procedure. Procedure methods that rebuild large prompts without caching cost more.
  number: HyperAgents with Opus-4.7 costs $9.50 per round on circle packing and $2.83 on autocorrelation.
  setup: Table 1, Best@3, 100-round cap.
  quote: "procedure-based methods can become expensive in long-horizon optimization by repeatedly constructing large prompts over an expanding search history without comparable caching"
  where: p.7
- Claim: Direct coding agents stop early because their internal stopping decision conflicts with the external budget. Keeping rounds, records and feedback outside the agent's loop fixes this.
  number: none. Codex's best round is 4 of 100 on kernel and 3 on circle packing in Table 1.
  setup: Table 1.
  quote: "an agent's internal stopping decision can conflict with the external evolution budget."
  where: p.7
- Claim: Ablation on kernel, three runs each. Removing the harness lets two of three runs reward-hack. Removing the meta-agent skills weakens search but causes no hacking.
  number: Full: 1138 cycles, no hack. Without skills: best 1407, with runs of 37, 99 and 65 rounds. Without harness: one run at 1167, two reward-hacking runs with N/A.
  setup: Appendix A, Table 3. Invalid evaluations are 16/100 for the full system.
  quote: "two of the three runs enter reward-hacking trajectories and fail to produce valid cycle results."
  where: p.8, Table 3 on p.13
- Claim: Progress after plateaus. Fixed-procedure methods flatten. AEvo revises the mechanism and jumps late in the run. Failed candidates become evidence for the next procedure edit.
  number: none
  setup: Kernel trajectories (Fig. 3). ARC-AGI-2 case study (Fig. 4): procedures P0 to P6, best artifact 0.35 (7/20).
  quote: "failed candidates are not merely discarded; they become process-level evidence that helps the meta-agent decide how to revise the future evolution procedure."
  where: pp.8-9, p.19
- Claim: Harness design. The evaluator is isolated from both the evolution agent and the meta-agent. Every candidate is logged with score, trace, failure and cost. The meta-agent follows one skill. It picks exactly one causal intervention per boundary and may not edit `candidates/` or call the evaluator.
  number: none
  setup: Section 4.1 and Appendix C.2.3.
  quote: "agents can submit candidates, but they cannot inspect evaluator internals, access hidden benchmark artifacts, or directly write official scores."
  where: p.5, p.15 ("Forbidden: edit `candidates/`; call `oer-eval eval` directly; bypass the gateway or evaluator")
- Claim: Coarse-grained intervention. One meta-edit governs a whole segment of evolution, with an iteration budget and stopping conditions. The meta-agent can extend a productive segment or stop an unproductive one.
  number: none
  setup: Section 4.
  quote: "one meta-edit can govern a segment of future evolution rather than a single candidate."
  where: p.4
- Claim: The evolved object in agent mode is a layered harness, not a prompt: task skill, per-session goal, persistent "family map" with falsified hypotheses and "Do not repeat" entries, support utilities, and structured session notes written back.
  number: the family map records session 9 reaching 1140 cycles, with the explicit-family port worth -597 cycles.
  setup: Appendix C.3.2.
  quote: "the evolved agent harness is not a single prompt edit. It is a layered control structure"
  where: pp.17-19
- Claim: The evolved ARC-AGI-2 procedure passes diagnostics from alternative candidates to the optimizer. It labels lower-scoring references "ANTI-EXAMPLE" and asks for one theory and the smallest probing edit.
  number: none
  setup: Appendix C.3.1.
  quote: "evolution changes the evidence presented to the optimizer and the way that evidence is structured, not only the candidate artifact being scored."
  where: p.17

LIMITS
- Conceded: the conclusion says future work should study "cheaper meta-intervention strategies" and "safer deployment". There is no dedicated limitations section.
- The 26% figure is for AEvo Procedure on 2 benchmarks only. Agent-based AEvo is not run on Terminal-Bench or ARC-AGI-2.
- Baselines differ by table: five procedure baselines on the benchmarks, but agents and OpenEvolve/HyperAgents on the open-ended tasks.
- Small samples: 3 runs, Best@3 on open-ended tasks (a best-of metric), 20 rounds on the benchmarks, 100 on the open-ended tasks.
- The gain is confounded with spend. The authors themselves describe it as scaling optimization-time reasoning at about 3x cost.
- Circle packing is essentially saturated: every method reaches about 2.6359.
- The ablation covers only the kernel task. The authors report a single run per cell, and only 3 runs for the ablated variants.
- Every model used is from the 2026 frontier set (Opus-4.7, GPT-5.4, Gemini-3-Flash). Results may not transfer to weaker models.
- Not shown: the meta-agent's own failure modes, such as bad edits that degrade performance.
- Not shown: any experiment with more than one level of meta-editing, so it is not recursive self-improvement.
- The meta-agent and evaluator are fixed, and the meta-agent does not edit its own skill within the experiments.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Procedure-based evolution: AlphaEvolve (Novikov 2025), OpenEvolve (Sharma 2025), AFlow (Zhang 2024), SimpleTES (Ye 2026), TTS-Discover (Yuksekgonul 2026), ASI-Evolve (Xu 2026).
- Agent-based evolution: Karpathy autoresearch (2026), CORAL (Qu 2026).
- Prompt optimization: DSPy (Khattab 2024), SPO (Xiang 2025), TextGrad (Yuksekgonul 2024), GEPA (Agrawal 2025).
- Self-modifying agents: ADAS (Hu 2024), Darwin Gödel Machine (Zhang 2025), Huxley-Gödel Machine (Wang 2025), HyperAgents (Zhang 2026).
- Meta-evolution of memory: MemEvolve (Zhang 2025), ALMA (Xiong 2026).
- Meta-learning: Learning to reinforcement learn (Wang 2016), Evolved Policy Gradients (Houthooft 2018).
- Agent scaffolds: ReAct (Yao 2022), Claude Code, Codex.

The paper contrasts itself with HyperAgents, which internalizes meta-improvement inside a self-modifying program. AEvo instead edits from outside, through a harness that governs the evaluator and records.

CODE (verbatim, Appendix)
- Meta-agent skill core loop and hard rules (p.15):
  `Read -> Attribute -> Choose Action -> Run Inner-Agent -> Record`
  `Allowed: write sessions/_next_goal.md; edit skill/evolve_skill.md; launch inner-agent through python -m evolver.cli run-inner-agent`
  `Forbidden: edit candidates/; call oer-eval eval directly; bypass the gateway or evaluator`
- Seed procedure (p.14): `BestByScoreSelection` picks the best valid candidate as parent, then `LLMRewriteOptimization` does a single rewrite. The editable surface is Selection and Optimization.
- Evolved ARC prompt tail (p.16): `"Form ONE specific theory about the current failures and test the smallest edit that directly probes that theory."`
- Agent skill (p.17): `## Don't stop early. While 'Session Evals Remaining > 0' you do not get to exit.`
- Session notes closing line (p.19): `One specific, falsifiable hypothesis for session 8.`
- Cost formula (p.14): `$/R = (1/R) Σ_r [p_in n_in(r) + p_cache n_cache(r) + p_out n_out(r)]`

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): procedure-based evolution, agent-based evolution, and AEvo's view of evolution as an environment. Shows where the meta-agent sits.
- Fig 2 (p.5): AEvo architecture. A protected evaluator, evidence store, `workspace/procedure/` and `meta/notes.md`, and the Πr to Πr+1 edit. It also shows the `notes.md` family map with "Falsified" and "Do not repeat" entries.
- Fig 3 (p.8): kernel trajectories for 8 methods over 100 iterations, and AEvo extended to 200 iterations. Shows plateau-breaking jumps.
- Fig 4 (p.9): ARC-AGI-2 case study of procedures P0-P6 with breakthrough and failed candidates. Concrete example of meta-edits.
- Tables 1-3 (pp.7, 13): the numeric results.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Table cells are concatenated in the extraction, so some values are my reading rather than directly quotable. Examples: "2.63592 0.34" is score 2.6359, best round 2, $0.34. "53.8747.012" is Terminal-Bench 53.8 (round 7) and ARC 47.0 (round 12). "100113899 16/100" is 100 rounds, 1138 cycles, best round 99, 16/100 invalid.
- Codex autocorrelation cost reads as $0.04, which looks odd next to the others. Check the PDF image before citing it.
- Table 2's ARC-AGI-2 score of 47.0 (Avg@3) differs from the 0.35 (7/20) best artifact in the Appendix. They are different metrics, but the paper does not reconcile them.
- I did not run the figure-caption script, so figure captions come from the extracted text only.
